hints: Focus on what actually changes the mass of the whole molecule when C and H have only one isotope each.
Work out the nucleon numbers of the two bromine isotopes using atomic number 35 plus 44 and 46 neutrons.
List the different ways to pick three bromine atoms from two types, then check how many different total masses that gives.
walkthrough:
**Find the mass numbers of the bromine isotopes**

Bromine has atomic number 35, so protons = 35. Add neutrons to get nucleon number.

$$^{79}\text{Br} = 35 + 44 \quad \text{and} \quad ^{81}\text{Br} = 35 + 46$$

**Fix the light part of the molecule**

$^{12}\text{C}$ and $^{1}\text{H}$ have no other common isotopes here, so they always contribute the same mass.

$$M(^{12}\text{C}^{1}\text{H}) = 12 + 1 = 13$$

**List all combinations of three bromine atoms**

With two types and three positions, order does not matter for mass, only how many of each type. There are just four distinct sets.

$$ (79,79,79), \; (79,79,81), \; (79,81,81), \; (81,81,81) $$

**Convert combinations to molecular ion masses**

Add 13 to the sum of the three bromine masses. Each combination gives a different $M_r$.

$$M_r = 13 + \text{sum of 3 Br masses} = 250, 252, 254, 256$$
So ignoring fragments, you see 4 molecular ion peaks.

options.A: 2 is the number of bromine isotopes, not the number of molecular masses. With three Br atoms in one molecule, the isotopes can mix in more than two ways.
options.B: 3 would be correct for a molecule with two Br atoms, where you get n+1 = 3 peaks. Here there are three Br atoms, so there is one more combination.
options.C: Correct. The four combinations give $^{12}\text{C}^{1}\text{H}^{79}\text{Br}_{3}$ at 250, $^{12}\text{C}^{1}\text{H}^{79}\text{Br}_{2}^{81}\text{Br}$ at 252, $^{12}\text{C}^{1}\text{H}^{79}\text{Br}^{81}\text{Br}_{2}$ at 254, and $^{12}\text{C}^{1}\text{H}^{81}\text{Br}_{3}$ at 256.
options.D: 6 comes from counting order as different, for example treating 79,79,81 and 79,81,79 as different peaks. In mass spectrometry only total mass matters, so those are the same peak.
